Open Start and type your company name and your own numbers in the yellow cells: safety days, the days of stock to hold, the count gap you accept, the supplier score you want and the most you want to hold in materials.

Material stock lists the 34 materials with the stock on hand, the reorder point (the stock level at which you order again) and the average use a day. Days of cover, the run-out date and a suggested order quantity fill in.

Purchase orders records every order to a supplier with the expected date. Fill in the received date when the goods arrive: the days late, the lead time and the date to pay fill in. An open order past its expected date shows as late.

Each delivery gets a lot number (a lot is one delivery of a material with its own lot number). Lots ranks the lots in first in first out order, so the oldest lot is opened first, and warns of a use-by date.
Use the Receiving log at the door: type the quantity ordered and received and the condition. A shortfall or a damaged delivery shows at once and you can send the supplier a message.

Stock counts compares the system quantity with the quantity on the shelf. The gap, its value and a tolerance check fill in. Stock adjustments records every correction with its reason and who approved it.
Waste and write-offs records every spill, expired lot and failed batch. Supplier issues records late, short and damaged deliveries and invoice problems with the days open.
Supplier prices keeps every price change. Supplier scorecards turns the orders and the issues of the last 12 months into one score for each supplier.
Finished stock and Packaging stock show the days of cover of products, jars, boxes and labels. The Reorder list holds the weekly orders with their value.
Use the 14 calculators before you order: reorder point, days of cover, pack size, batch need, lot picker, count variance, price comparison, landed cost, safety stock, shelf life and lead time.
Read the Stock and Purchasing Dashboard and the Charts every week: stock value, days of cover, late orders, spend, waste, count variances and supplier issues.
Order profit, packing, shipping and returns in one workbook
Order profit, packing, shipping and returns for candle and soap makers
Order profit after fee, shipping and packaging
each order shows its goods cost, channel fee, shipping paid and packaging, so profit and margin are numbers and a loss-maker turns red
each order waiting to be packed shows its packer, its due date, the hours it has waited and a flag when it is due today or overdue, so nothing sits for days
the average order, the threshold, the shipping cost and the orders a month show what free shipping costs and the extra spend a customer needs to reach it
every code shows its uses, the discount given, the order value and its end date, so you see which codes pay for themselves
each return has its reason, product, refund and the days to resolve, and each refund its approval and share of the order
damaged, lost and late parcels with the claim amount, the status and the days open, so no claim is forgotten before the courier deadline
the days you promise against the days parcels really take for each country and method, with a late flag, so the delivery message tells the truth
occasion, items to wrap, the length of the card message and the wrapping cost for every gift order
the day and time a message came and the day and time you replied give the hours to reply and a check against your target
orders a day, minutes per order and packing staff give the hours needed, the overtime and the people you need before the busy weeks
Shipping method and weight band prices
twelve rate rows show the price you charge against the courier cost and flag every band where you lose money
